text: Paris, France: best visited April-June and September-October. Top sights: Eiffel Tower, Louvre, Notre-Dame, Montmartre, Seine river cruise. Average daily budget mid-range: 120-180 EUR. Tipping is included in restaurant bills (service compris).

Tokyo, Japan: spring (cherry blossom, late March-early April) and autumn are peak. Must-see: Senso-ji, Shibuya Crossing, teamLab, Tsukiji Outer Market, Meiji Shrine, Akihabara. Get a Suica/Pasmo card for transit. Budget mid-range: 12000-18000 JPY/day.

Rome, Italy: shoulder seasons (April, May, October) recommended. Highlights: Colosseum, Vatican Museums + Sistine Chapel, Trevi Fountain, Pantheon, Trastevere neighborhood. Book Vatican and Colosseum tickets in advance. Local food: cacio e pepe, supplì, gelato.

Bali, Indonesia: dry season May-September is ideal. Areas to base in: Ubud (culture, rice terraces), Seminyak (beaches, nightlife), Canggu (digital nomads, surf), Uluwatu (cliffs). Don't miss: Tegallalang rice terraces, Tirta Empul, Mount Batur sunrise hike.

New York City, USA: spring and fall most pleasant. Don't miss: Central Park, Statue of Liberty, MoMA, Brooklyn Bridge walk, Broadway show, food in Lower East Side & Queens. Subway is fastest; OMNY contactless tap works on most cards. Tip 18-20% in restaurants.

Barcelona, Spain: best May-June and September. Iconic sights: Sagrada Familia, Park Güell, Casa Batlló, La Boqueria market, Gothic Quarter, Barceloneta beach. Day trip: Montserrat. Watch for pickpockets on La Rambla and metro.

Reykjavik, Iceland: northern lights season Sep-March; midnight sun summer. Ring Road covers all major sights in 7-10 days: Golden Circle, South Coast (Seljalandsfoss, Skógafoss, Reynisfjara, Jökulsárlón), Highlands. Rent a car; F-roads need 4x4.

Marrakech, Morocco: October-April is comfortable. Stay in a riad in the Medina. Visit Jemaa el-Fnaa, Bahia Palace, Majorelle Garden, Ben Youssef Madrasa. Day trips: Atlas Mountains, Essaouira coast. Bargain in souks; aim for 30-50% of opening price.

Bangkok, Thailand: cool/dry season Nov-Feb. Must-do: Grand Palace, Wat Pho reclining Buddha, Chatuchak weekend market, Chao Phraya river dinner cruise, street food (Yaowarat). Use BTS/MRT to skip traffic. Wear modest clothing in temples.

Cape Town, South Africa: Nov-April warm and dry. Highlights: Table Mountain (cable car or Platteklip Gorge hike), V&A Waterfront, Robben Island, Cape Point peninsula drive, Boulders Beach penguins. Wine country in Stellenbosch and Franschhoek.

Dubai, UAE: October-April for outdoor activities. See: Burj Khalifa, Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Mall, Old Dubai (Bastakiya, Gold Souk), desert safari with dune bashing. Friday is the holy day; some businesses open late. Alcohol only in licensed venues.

Cusco & Machu Picchu, Peru: dry season May-October. Acclimatize 2-3 days in Cusco (3400m altitude). Buy Machu Picchu tickets in advance; choose Circuit 2 for classic views. Sacred Valley day trips: Pisac, Ollantaytambo, Maras salt mines.

Travel tip: Book international flights 6-8 weeks in advance for best prices on average; domestic 3-6 weeks. Tuesday/Wednesday departures often cheaper than weekends. Use incognito mode when comparing fares.

Travel tip: For Schengen visa, apply 3-6 weeks before travel through the consulate of the country where you'll spend the most days. Required: travel insurance with 30000 EUR coverage, proof of accommodation, financial means, return flight.

Travel tip: Pack one carry-on outfit + essentials in case checked luggage is delayed. Roll clothes (saves space). Use packing cubes. Keep valuables, medication, electronics in carry-on. Bring a universal adapter.

Solo female travel safety: research neighborhood reputation before booking, avoid arriving after dark, share itinerary with someone at home, use reputable ride-hail apps over street taxis, dress to fit local norms in conservative regions.

Budget travel: hostels in Europe avg 25-45 EUR/night; SE Asia 8-15 USD. Eat where locals eat (rule of thumb: away from main squares). Trains often cheaper than flights short-haul in Europe. Free walking tours in most cities (tip the guide).

Family travel: book apartments/Airbnbs over hotels for kitchen + space. Look for cities with extensive public transport so you don't need car seats. Prioritize neighborhoods with parks. Pack a small first-aid kit.

Sustainable travel: choose direct flights when possible (takeoff/landing burn most fuel), use trains for short-haul, stay 3+ nights per stop, support locally-owned businesses, refill water bottles, avoid wildlife attractions involving captive animals.

Visa-free travel for EU citizens: 90 days within 180 to most of the world's tourist destinations. Major exceptions requiring eVisa or visa: Australia (eVisitor/ETA), USA (ESTA), Canada (eTA), Brazil (varies), India (eVisa), China.
